items.stem: Define the term 'quantitative location factors'.
items.answer: Factors that can be measured in money terms, such as site and building costs, labour costs, transport costs and government grants.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, factors that can be measured in money terms, such as site and building costs, labour costs, transport costs and government grants. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why qualitative factors are important in location decisions.
items.answer: Some factors, such as the availability of skilled staff, local attitudes, safety and quality of life, affect long-run success but cannot be measured in money.
items.markingKey: 1 mark examples; 1 mark long-run significance. [2]

items.stem: Explain one limitation of using weighted scoring to choose a location.
items.answer: Weights and scores are subjective, so managers can bias the result; it may ignore factors not included.
items.markingKey: 1 mark subjectivity; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem: Based in Toronto, Maple Learning Inc. (private limited company) runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. The business has around 260 employees. Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Explain the quantitative and qualitative factors Maple Learning should consider when choosing a new site.
items.answer: Points to develop for Maple Learning: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants; qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for online tutoring subscriptions; scope for future expansion.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Maple Learning: education technology, about 260 employees, private limited company in Canada; venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Maple Learning, e.g. qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for online tutoring subscriptions; scope for future expansion. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor. Muscat Dates & Co. LLC, a family-owned limited company in Oman with about 160 employees, processes, packs and exports dates and date syrup. Explain the quantitative and qualitative factors Muscat Dates should consider when choosing a new site.
items.answer: Points to develop for Muscat Dates: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants; qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for packed dates and date syrup; scope for future expansion.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Muscat Dates: food processing, about 160 employees, family-owned limited company in Oman; three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Muscat Dates, e.g. qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for packed dates and date syrup; scope for future expansion. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Manila, IslaConnect Inc. (private limited company) runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia. The business has around 2,600 employees. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Evaluate the most important factor for IslaConnect when choosing the location of a new site.
items.answer: For: costs of land and labour; access to customers; availability of skilled labour. Against: qualitative factors such as quality of life; government incentives; infrastructure and logistics. Judgement: the decision for IslaConnect depends mainly on the nature of its call-centre and back-office services, and also on whether the site serves local or export markets.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (IslaConnect: business process outsourcing, about 2,600 employees, private limited company in the Philippines; clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. costs of land and labour; access to customers; availability of skilled labour; arguments against, e.g. qualitative factors such as quality of life; government incentives; infrastructure and logistics. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the nature of its call-centre and back-office services; whether the site serves local or export markets; its long-term strategy. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to IslaConnect, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which business term is described here: "Factors that can be measured in money terms, such as site and building costs, labour costs, transport costs and government grants."
items.answer: quantitative location factors
items.markingKey: This is the definition of quantitative location factors.

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd is a private limited company based in Accra, Ghana. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars and employs about 450 people. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Explain one advantage to Gold Coast Cocoa of moving its main operation to a cheaper out-of-town site.
items.answer: Lower rent and labour costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. lower rent and labour costs; room to expand; possible government grants. 1 mark: explained in the context of Gold Coast Cocoa (confectionery). [2]

items.stem: Explain why break-even analysis is useful when comparing two possible sites.
items.answer: Each site has different fixed and variable costs; comparing break-even outputs shows which site becomes profitable at lower output and the risk at each.
items.markingKey: 1 mark different costs; 1 mark comparison of risk/profit. [2]

items.stem: Desert Bloom Hotels plc is a public limited company based in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. It operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels and employs about 3,100 people. Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Explain two benefits to Desert Bloom of moving its main operation to a cheaper out-of-town site, using the case to support your answer.
items.answer: Lower rent and labour costs; room to expand.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark application to Desert Bloom: hospitality, 3,100 employees). Points: lower rent and labour costs; room to expand; possible government grants; relocation costs and disruption; loss of skilled staff who will not move; further from customers or suppliers. [4]

items.stem: Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd is choosing between two sites. Factors, weights and scores out of 10 are — labour costs (weight 0.4): site X 4, site Y 9; site cost (weight 0.3): site X 7, site Y 5; transport links (weight 0.2): site X 8, site Y 7; government grants (weight 0.1): site X 4, site Y 7. Calculate the weighted score for each site and state which site should be chosen on this basis.
items.answer: X 5.7, Y 7.2: site Y

items.stem: Savanna Fresh Ltd is choosing between two sites. Factors, weights and scores out of 10 are — labour costs (weight 0.35): site X 8, site Y 8; site cost (weight 0.3): site X 4, site Y 9; skilled labour (weight 0.2): site X 4, site Y 4; transport links (weight 0.15): site X 7, site Y 5. Calculate the weighted score for each site and state which site should be chosen on this basis.
items.answer: X 5.85, Y 7.05: site Y

items.stem: One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Han River Games Co., a private limited company in South Korea with about 340 employees, develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases. Explain the quantitative and qualitative factors Han River Games should consider when choosing a new site.
items.answer: Points to develop for Han River Games: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants; qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for mobile games; scope for future expansion.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Han River Games: video game development, about 340 employees, private limited company in South Korea; one game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Han River Games, e.g. qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for mobile games; scope for future expansion. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Lagos, Lagos Bites Ltd (private limited company) produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. The business has around 700 employees. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. (a) Define 'weighted scoring (location)'. (b) Explain one advantage to Lagos Bites of moving its main operation to a cheaper out-of-town site.
items.answer: (a) A decision-making technique in which each location factor is given a weight according to its importance, each site is scored on each factor, and the weighted scores are totalled. (b) Lower rent and labour costs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (lower rent and labour costs; room to expand; possible government grants), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Lagos Bites [3]

items.stem: Many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities. Lanka Tea Estates plc, a public limited company in Sri Lanka with about 5,000 employees, grows, processes and packs tea on its own estates. Discuss whether Lanka Tea should base its location decision mainly on weighted scoring results.
items.answer: For: systematic and transparent; combines several factors; reflects managers' priorities. Against: weights and scores are subjective; may ignore key risks; quantitative methods like investment appraisal also needed. Judgement: the decision for Lanka Tea depends mainly on how the weights were chosen, and also on the closeness of the scores.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Lanka Tea: agriculture and food, about 5,000 employees, public limited company in Sri Lanka; many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities). AO3 Analysis [6]: arguments for, e.g. systematic and transparent; combines several factors; reflects managers' priorities; arguments against, e.g. weights and scores are subjective; may ignore key risks; quantitative methods like investment appraisal also needed. AO4 Evaluation [8]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how the weights were chosen; the closeness of the scores; the cost of a wrong decision. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Lanka Tea, not a generic one. [20]

items.stem: Define the term 'offshoring'.
items.answer: Moving some business activities, such as production or customer service, to another country, either within the firm or by outsourcing to a foreign supplier.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, moving some business activities, such as production or customer service, to another country, either within the firm or by outsourcing to a foreign supplier. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two reasons why a business might offshore its production.
items.answer: Lower labour and land costs; to be close to growing foreign markets; to avoid tariffs; access to raw materials or skills.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark reason, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain why offshoring customer service may harm a business.
items.answer: Language, cultural and time-zone differences can reduce service quality and customer satisfaction, damaging the brand.
items.markingKey: 1 mark problem; 1 mark effect. [2]

items.stem: Based in Auckland, Kiwi Trails Ltd (private limited company) runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours. The business has around 90 employees. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Explain how a decision to reshore operations could affect Kiwi Trails.
items.answer: Points to develop for Kiwi Trails: reshoring brings activities back home; higher labour costs but lower transport and inventory costs; better quality control and faster response; possible marketing benefit and government support.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: reshoring brings activities back home. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Kiwi Trails: tourism, about 90 employees, private limited company in New Zealand; bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Kiwi Trails, e.g. higher labour costs but lower transport and inventory costs; better quality control and faster response; possible marketing benefit and government support. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd is a private limited company based in Accra, Ghana. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars and employs about 450 people. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Explain the factors Gold Coast Cocoa should consider before moving production abroad.
items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: labour, land and transport costs; trade barriers and exchange rates; political stability and legal system; quality, ethics and supply-chain risk.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: labour, land and transport costs. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Gold Coast Cocoa: confectionery, about 450 employees, private limited company in Ghana; world cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Gold Coast Cocoa, e.g. trade barriers and exchange rates; political stability and legal system; quality, ethics and supply-chain risk. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd, a private limited company in South Africa with about 140 employees, brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets. Evaluate whether Cape Brew should offshore part of its operations.
items.answer: For: lower costs; access to new markets; avoids trade barriers. Against: quality and control problems; ethical and reputational risks; exchange-rate and political risk. Judgement: the decision for Cape Brew depends mainly on the size of the cost saving, and also on the importance of speed and quality to customers.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Cape Brew: beverages, about 140 employees, private limited company in South Africa; demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. lower costs; access to new markets; avoids trade barriers; arguments against, e.g. quality and control problems; ethical and reputational risks; exchange-rate and political risk. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the size of the cost saving; the importance of speed and quality to customers; its experience of managing abroad. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Cape Brew, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which is the most likely reason for a business to reshore production?
options: Rising wages and transport costs abroad combined with a need for faster delivery
items.answer: Rising wages and transport costs abroad combined with a need for faster delivery
items.markingKey: Rising wages and transport costs abroad combined with a need for faster delivery. Reshoring happens when the cost advantage of offshoring shrinks or speed and control matter more.

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd is a private limited company based in Accra, Ghana. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars and employs about 450 people. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Explain one disadvantage to Gold Coast Cocoa of reshoring production to Ghana.
items.answer: Higher labour costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. higher labour costs; cost of building new capacity; skills shortages at home. 1 mark: explained in the context of Gold Coast Cocoa (confectionery). [2]

items.stem: Explain how reshoring could improve a business's supply chain.
items.answer: Shorter distances reduce lead times and transport costs, make just-in-time easier and reduce the risk of disruption.
items.markingKey: 1 mark shorter/faster; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem: Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Maple Learning Inc., a private limited company in Canada with about 260 employees, runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. Explain two reasons why reshoring production to Canada might not benefit Maple Learning.
items.answer: Higher labour costs; cost of building new capacity.
items.markingKey: For each point: 1 mark identification, 1 mark explanation applied to Maple Learning. Advantages: faster delivery and better control; "made in" branding advantage; lower supply-chain risk. Disadvantages: higher labour costs; cost of building new capacity; skills shortages at home. [4]

items.stem: Producing a product abroad costs $9 labour and $11 materials per unit, plus $4 transport per unit. What is the total unit cost?

Lumen Robotics plc compares making a product at home and abroad. Home: labour $16 and materials $10 per unit. Abroad: labour $8 and materials $10 per unit, plus shipping of $2.5 per unit and a 10% import tariff on the production cost (labour + materials) when the goods return. Calculate the unit cost of each option.
items.answer: Home $26.00, abroad $22.30

items.stem: Andes Textil SA compares making a product at home and abroad. Home: labour $16 and materials $6 per unit. Abroad: labour $8 and materials $7 per unit, plus shipping of $4 per unit and a 5% import tariff on the production cost (labour + materials) when the goods return. Calculate the unit cost of each option and the annual saving for 50,000 units.
items.answer: Home $22.00, abroad $19.75; saving $112,500

items.stem: Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd, a private limited company in Thailand with about 1,100 employees, produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores. (a) Define 'offshoring'. (b) Explain one advantage to Siam Ready Meals of reshoring production to Thailand.
items.answer: (a) Moving some business activities, such as production or customer service, to another country, either within the firm or by outsourcing to a foreign supplier. (b) Faster delivery and better control.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (faster delivery and better control; "made in" branding advantage; lower supply-chain risk), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Siam Ready Meals [3]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Discuss whether reshoring is likely to become more common for businesses such as Pearl Logistics.
items.answer: For: rising wages in former low-cost countries; supply-chain disruptions; automation reduces labour cost advantage. Against: labour costs abroad still much lower; established supplier networks; growing markets are abroad. Judgement: the decision for Pearl Logistics depends mainly on the industry, and also on the cost of automation.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Pearl Logistics: logistics, about 1,500 employees, private limited company in Qatar; large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. rising wages in former low-cost countries; supply-chain disruptions; automation reduces labour cost advantage; arguments against, e.g. labour costs abroad still much lower; established supplier networks; growing markets are abroad. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the industry; the cost of automation; government incentives. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Pearl Logistics, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Define the term 'optimum scale of production'.
items.answer: The scale of operation at which average (unit) cost is at its lowest.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the scale of operation at which average (unit) cost is at its lowest. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: At the optimum scale of production, average cost is
items.answer: at its lowest point
items.markingKey: at its lowest point. Optimum scale = minimum average cost.

items.stem: Explain why a business may choose to operate below its optimum scale.
items.answer: Demand may be too small to support optimum output, finance may be limited, or the owners may want to keep control and flexibility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reason; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Based in Lima, Andes Textil SA (family-owned private company) makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan. The business has around 320 employees. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Explain the factors that influence the optimum scale of production for Andes Textil.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andes Textil: optimum scale minimises average cost; size of market demand for alpaca knitwear; availability of finance and technology; management ability to control a larger operation.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: optimum scale minimises average cost. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Andes Textil: textile manufacturing, about 320 employees, family-owned private company in Peru; the founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Andes Textil, e.g. size of market demand for alpaca knitwear; availability of finance and technology; management ability to control a larger operation. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Hanoi, Mekong Furniture JSC (joint stock company) makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe. The business has around 1,200 employees. A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. Discuss whether Mekong Furniture should aim to operate at the minimum efficient scale for its industry.
items.answer: For: lowest unit costs; price competitiveness; higher margins. Against: market may be too small; loss of flexibility; niche strategy may suit it better. Judgement: the decision for Mekong Furniture depends mainly on its competitive strategy, and also on the size of its market.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Mekong Furniture: furniture manufacturing, about 1,200 employees, joint stock company in Vietnam; a major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six). AO3 Analysis [2]: arguments for, e.g. lowest unit costs; price competitiveness; higher margins; arguments against, e.g. market may be too small; loss of flexibility; niche strategy may suit it better. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its competitive strategy; the size of its market; the cost structure of the industry. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Mekong Furniture, not a generic one. [8]

items.stem: Explain how the optimum scale of production differs between industries.
items.answer: Industries with high fixed costs and specialised equipment (e.g. car making) have a large minimum efficient scale; services with personal contact (e.g. hairdressing) have a small one.
items.markingKey: 1 mark link to fixed costs/technology; 1 mark examples. [2]

items.stem: Maple Learning Inc. estimates its annual total costs at different scales of output — 40,000 units: total cost $780,000; 80,000 units: total cost $1,220,000; 120,000 units: total cost $1,820,000; 160,000 units: total cost $2,580,000; 200,000 units: total cost $3,500,000. Calculate the average cost at each output and identify the optimum scale.
items.answer: Optimum 120,000 units at $15.17 per unit

items.stem: Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd, a private limited company in Thailand with about 1,100 employees, produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores. Evaluate whether Siam Ready Meals should increase its scale of operation.
items.answer: For: economies of scale; meets rising demand; stronger market position. Against: diseconomies of scale; investment risk; demand may not grow. Judgement: the decision for Siam Ready Meals depends mainly on forecast demand, and also on current capacity utilisation.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. items.stem: Which is a qualitative factor in a location decision?
options: The quality of local schools for managers' families
The monthly rent of the site

items.stem: Tejo Mobility SA is a public limited company based in Lisbon, Portugal. It assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union and employs about 600 people. Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. (a) Define 'industrial inertia'. (b) Explain one advantage to Tejo Mobility of moving its main operation to a cheaper out-of-town site.
items.answer: (a) The tendency of firms to stay in their original location even when the original advantages have disappeared. (b) Lower rent and labour costs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (lower rent and labour costs; room to expand; possible government grants), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Tejo Mobility [3]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'reshoring'?
options: A decision-making technique in which each location factor is given a weight according to its importance, each site is scored on each factor, and the weighted scores are totalled.
Non-numerical factors in a location decision, such as quality of life, safety, attitudes of the local community and management preferences.
Bringing production or other activities back to the home country after they had been moved abroad.
Actual output as a percentage of the maximum possible output: actual output ÷ maximum capacity × 100.
items.answer: Bringing production or other activities back to the home country after they had been moved abroad.
items.markingKey: reshoring: Bringing production or other activities back to the home country after they had been moved abroad.

items.stem: Based in Karachi, Indus Sports Goods Ltd (private limited company) makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. The business has around 950 employees. A rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices. Explain one disadvantage to Indus Sports of reshoring production to Pakistan.
items.answer: Higher labour costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. higher labour costs; cost of building new capacity; skills shortages at home. 1 mark: explained in the context of Indus Sports (sports equipment manufacturing). [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain how reshoring could improve a business's supply chain. (b) Explain two reasons why a business might offshore its production.
items.answer: (a) Shorter distances reduce lead times and transport costs, make just-in-time easier and reduce the risk of disruption. (b) Lower labour and land costs; to be close to growing foreign markets; to avoid tariffs; access to raw materials or skills.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark shorter/faster; 1 mark consequence. [2] (b) 2 × (1 mark reason, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Nusantara Apparel Tbk is a public limited company based in Jakarta, Indonesia. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands and employs about 4,000 people. A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Explain how a decision to reshore operations could affect Nusantara Apparel.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: reshoring brings activities back home; higher labour costs but lower transport and inventory costs; better quality control and faster response; possible marketing benefit and government support.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: reshoring brings activities back home. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, about 4,000 employees, public limited company in Indonesia; a global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Nusantara Apparel, e.g. higher labour costs but lower transport and inventory costs; better quality control and faster response; possible marketing benefit and government support. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Lagos Bites Ltd compares making a product at home and abroad. Home: labour $14 and materials $8 per unit. Abroad: labour $4.2 and materials $8 per unit, plus shipping of $3 per unit and a 10% import tariff on the production cost (labour + materials) when the goods return. Calculate the unit cost of each option.
items.answer: Home $22.00, abroad $16.42

items.stem: Based in Madrid, Iberia Moda SA (public limited company) runs 180 fast-fashion clothing stores and an online shop. The business has around 6,000 employees. Online sales are growing quickly while sales in its high-street stores are falling. Explain the factors Iberia Moda should consider before moving production abroad.
items.answer: Points to develop for Iberia Moda: labour, land and transport costs; trade barriers and exchange rates; political stability and legal system; quality, ethics and supply-chain risk.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: labour, land and transport costs. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Iberia Moda: clothing retail, about 6,000 employees, public limited company in Spain; online sales are growing quickly while sales in its high-street stores are falling). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Iberia Moda, e.g. trade barriers and exchange rates; political stability and legal system; quality, ethics and supply-chain risk. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Pearl Logistics WLL, a private limited company in Qatar with about 1,500 employees, provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. (a) Define 'multi-site location'. (b) Explain one advantage to Pearl Logistics of offshoring production to a lower-cost country.
items.answer: (a) Operating from several locations, possibly in different countries, rather than from one site. (b) Lower labour and site costs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (lower labour and site costs; closer to new markets; may avoid tariffs), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Pearl Logistics [3]

items.stem: Which business term is described here: "The scale of operation at which average (unit) cost is at its lowest."
items.answer: optimum scale of production
items.markingKey: This is the definition of optimum scale of production.

items.stem: Explain why average costs may rise if a business expands beyond its optimum scale.
items.answer: Diseconomies of scale such as poor coordination, slow communication and low motivation increase costs per unit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark diseconomies; 1 mark effect on unit cost. [2]

items.stem: Desert Bloom Hotels plc is a public limited company based in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. It operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels and employs about 3,100 people. Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Explain why increasing its scale of production by 50% could be both an opportunity and a threat for Desert Bloom.
items.answer: Opportunity: economies of scale cut unit costs. Threat: risk of diseconomies of scale.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark application to Desert Bloom: hospitality, 3,100 employees). Points: economies of scale cut unit costs; able to meet growing demand; stronger bargaining power; risk of diseconomies of scale; spare capacity if demand falls; large capital investment. [4]

items.stem: Nusantara Apparel Tbk is a public limited company based in Jakarta, Indonesia. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands and employs about 4,000 people. A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Explain the factors that influence the optimum scale of production for Nusantara Apparel.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: optimum scale minimises average cost; size of market demand for sportswear; availability of finance and technology; management ability to control a larger operation.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: optimum scale minimises average cost. items.stem: A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. Mekong Furniture JSC, a joint stock company in Vietnam with about 1,200 employees, makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe. Evaluate whether Mekong Furniture should increase its scale of operation.
items.answer: For: economies of scale; meets rising demand; stronger market position. Against: diseconomies of scale; investment risk; demand may not grow. Judgement: the decision for Mekong Furniture depends mainly on forecast demand, and also on current capacity utilisation.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Mekong Furniture: furniture manufacturing, about 1,200 employees, joint stock company in Vietnam; a major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. economies of scale; meets rising demand; stronger market position; arguments against, e.g. diseconomies of scale; investment risk; demand may not grow. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on forecast demand; current capacity utilisation; access to finance. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Mekong Furniture, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'qualitative location factors'?
options: Non-numerical factors in a location decision, such as quality of life, safety, attitudes of the local community and management preferences.
The tendency of firms to stay in their original location even when the original advantages have disappeared.
Factors that can be measured in money terms, such as site and building costs, labour costs, transport costs and government grants.
The maximum output that can be achieved using the resources currently available to a business.
items.answer: Non-numerical factors in a location decision, such as quality of life, safety, attitudes of the local community and management preferences.
items.markingKey: qualitative location factors: Non-numerical factors in a location decision, such as quality of life, safety, attitudes of the local community and management preferences.

items.stem: BatikPay Sdn Bhd is a private limited company based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops and employs about 210 people. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Explain one disadvantage to BatikPay of moving its main operation to a cheaper out-of-town site.
items.answer: Relocation costs and disruption.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. relocation costs and disruption; loss of skilled staff who will not move; further from customers or suppliers. 1 mark: explained in the context of BatikPay (financial technology). [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why qualitative factors are important in location decisions. (b) Explain why break-even analysis is useful when comparing two possible sites.
items.answer: (a) Some factors, such as the availability of skilled staff, local attitudes, safety and quality of life, affect long-run success but cannot be measured in money. (b) Each site has different fixed and variable costs; comparing break-even outputs shows which site becomes profitable at lower output and the risk at each.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark examples; 1 mark long-run significance. [2] (b) 1 mark different costs; 1 mark comparison of risk/profit. [2]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Explain the quantitative and qualitative factors Pearl Logistics should consider when choosing a new site.
items.answer: Points to develop for Pearl Logistics: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants; qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for freight and warehousing services; scope for future expansion.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants. AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Pearl Logistics, e.g. qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for freight and warehousing services; scope for future expansion. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Savanna Fresh Ltd is choosing between two sites. Factors, weights and scores out of 10 are — site cost (weight 0.4): site X 5, site Y 9; skilled labour (weight 0.3): site X 6, site Y 5; nearness to customers (weight 0.2): site X 8, site Y 9; transport links (weight 0.1): site X 4, site Y 6. Calculate the weighted score for each site and state which site should be chosen on this basis.
items.answer: X 5.8, Y 7.5: site Y

items.answer: Points to develop for Deccan Auto: quantitative: land, building, labour and transport costs, grants; qualitative: skills, local attitudes, infrastructure quality; access to customers and suppliers for brake and steering components; scope for future expansion.

items.stem: Based in Auckland, Kiwi Trails Ltd (private limited company) runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours. The business has around 90 employees. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. (a) Define 'quantitative location factors'. (b) Evaluate the most important factor for Kiwi Trails when choosing the location of a new site.
items.answer: (a) Factors that can be measured in money terms, such as site and building costs, labour costs, transport costs and government grants. (b) For: costs of land and labour; access to customers; availability of skilled labour. Against: qualitative factors such as quality of life; government incentives; infrastructure and logistics. Judgement: the decision for Kiwi Trails depends mainly on the nature of its adventure tours, and also on whether the site serves local or export markets.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory.
